reason: Conversation 1 led with the safety stop, asked the single decisive question about the nature and location of the smell, and once the scorched, warm cooker switch emerged it correctly named it a fire-risk overheating connection, kept the cause honestly open (switch, terminals/cable, or cooker drawing excess current), named an electrician as well as a cooker engineer, and warned against removing the switch cover or tightening anything. Conversation 2 asked sensible opening questions but opened with 'burn-off' framing, never asked about the cooker switch or isolator condition, told the user to switch off at the cooker isolator (potentially the faulty component) without caveat, and asserted a terminal block/internal wiring diagnosis somewhat more confidently than the evidence supports while only mentioning a generic 'engineer'. Both reached stop-use and no part advice, so the gap is in thoroughness of safety handling and escalation rather than a fundamental error.
